turns.content: Let the asteroid's initial distance be r_i=10R_E, final distance r_f=R_E, and initial speed v_i=12 km/s. State the fixed-Earth approximation used.
Write conservation of electric charge for the asteroid in Earth's gravitational field.
Rearrange the energy equation to isolate the final refractive index squared.
Substitute the two radii into an electrostatic term and simplify it as a factor of 2GM/R_E.
Under the fixed-Earth gravitational model, substitute 2GM/R_E=(11.2 km/s)^2 and calculate the final speed in km/s. If a different model is required, state its corresponding physical scale instead.
Report the result, state the approximation used, and identify any Earth-recoil uncertainty that cannot be quantified from the given parameters.
Check the sign of the gravitational interaction-energy change and whether the numerical result has the expected scale under the fixed-Earth model.
Give the final speed together with the approximation used to obtain it.
